#1908. Arsenal make Premier League history by doing something no side has ever done to Liverpool at Anfield

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 07:21

Arsenal strengthened their position at the top of the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield.

Kai Havertz's first-half goal proved decisive, but Mikel Arteta's side also delivered another outstanding defensive performance.

In fact, the Gunners achieved something no visiting team had ever managed against Liverpool at Anfield in Premier League history.

According to The xG Philosophy, Arsenal conceded just 0.00 expected goals on target (xGOT) against Liverpool, a record low for a visiting team at Anfield in the Premier League era.

The statistic underlines the effectiveness of Arteta's defensive unit, particularly given the pressure Liverpool applied during the opening stages.

Arsenal took the lead in the 16th minute when Declan Rice delivered a dangerous ball across the face of goal, allowing Havertz to convert at the back post.

No team had ever done this to Liverpool at Anfield in Premier League history.

Liverpool responded with sustained pressure, with goalkeeper David Raya producing an important intervention to prevent Virgil van Dijk's flick-on from reaching Alexander Isak. Florian Wirtz also struck the crossbar with a free-kick as the hosts searched for an equaliser.

However, the Gunners' defensive organisation improved considerably after the interval, restricting Liverpool's opportunities and ensuring Raya was rarely seriously troubled.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's introduction helped the champions regain control late on, while Alisson denied Christos Tzolis a second goal with an excellent save.

The result secured Arsenal's first Premier League victory at Anfield since 2012 and moved them three points clear at the summit.

There is no doubt that Arsenal deserve enormous credit for their defensive display, but Liverpool's attacking numbers will concern Andoni Iraola.

The Reds have registered just 13.3 expected goals (xG) in the Premier League this season, ranking tenth in the division, while their 12 big chances created leave them joint-19th. They also rank eighth for touches inside the opposition box, ninth for shots on target per match and joint bottom for set-piece goals, having failed to score from one.

Alexander Isak has managed six goals in eight league appearances, but the striker has received limited service, while big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola have yet to deliver consistent end product.

Arsenal's defensive structure undoubtedly contributed to those struggles, but Liverpool cannot rely on facing opponents who allow them to create opportunities through sustained pressure.

Iraola's attacking approach has shown promise, particularly with the pace and intensity of their high press, but the lack of quality in the final third is becoming increasingly difficult to overlook.

Against Arsenal, the Gunners' defensive excellence was the main story. However, Liverpool's inability to turn promising attacking positions into genuine chances suggests there is still plenty of work for Iraola to do.

#1906. Agutter’s team hand Worthing first league defeat in 11 games

A goal from former Rebels striker Temi Babalola, an own goal by Jayden Moore and Charlie Carter’s penalty put the hosts at the base of an incredibly steep mountain, which they were unable to overcome in the second period against ex-boss Chris Agutter’s team.

After a productive display during midweek off the bench, Jordan Young was restored to the starting XI and was joined by Charley Kendall in attack, with Jack Wadham returning to the side to face his former team in place of Charlie Waller.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

From the first whistle, Sutton’s game plan was evident. The frontline looked to suffocate Adam Hinshelwood’s side in possession, with plenty of full-blooded challenges flying in to disrupt any sort of momentum. Indeed, by the time referee Harry Wager had blown for half-time, the Amber Army already had four players on a yellow card.

The tone was set in the early proceedings as Babalola was booked for a late challenge and Joel Colbran caught Carter late by the dugouts, sparking a brief melee between the players.

Agutter’s team were gaining plenty of territory and took a route one approach to find their first of three goals in the opening 45.

Possessing an enormous throw-in technique, Dan Urpens hurled the ball into the middle and with a congested box and a hideous glare from the sun in their eyes, Worthing failed to deal with the danger. Moore was the unfortunate man to turn the ball into his own net as the Southampton loanee’s header was misdirected beyond Seymour.

Worthing’s afternoon went from bad to worse just over five minutes later as Babalola came back to haunt his former employers. The lively Brandon Njoku profited after Joe Cook had lost flight of a pass upfield – teeing up the imposing striker, whose sweeping finish into the top corner was executed in a devastating manner.

An abject 12-minute spell was rounded off just after the half hour mark as Sutton scored their third. Neither Cook nor Moore took control of another long ball which allowed Njoku to anticipate the situation and punish the Reds again, as he won a penalty. Seymour tried to push the ball away from safety, but could only foul the forward and leave the referee to point to the penalty spot.

The Sussex Cat couldn’t atone for his error, as Carter kept his composure to send his penalty down the middle to cause the away end to burst into raptures.

It took until the latter stages of the first period for the hosts to muster a response, as sustained possession culminated with Cory Adjetey-Brew firing straight at Spike Brits.

Despite plenty of intent from the Mackerel Men after the restart, the scoreline remained 3-0 for the remainder of the tussle.

Razzaq Coleman De-Graft’s dipping shot from long range had the beating of Brits but landed on the roof of the net, while substitutes Emmerson Sutton and Daniel Isichei combined well, only for the latter to sidefoot a shot wide.

QPR loanee Sutton came closest to notching a consolation, with his powerful strike deviating through the air and crashing off the post.

Ultimately, it was a disappointing afternoon to end Worthing’s ten-game unbeaten run in the National League. They now have a break from league action before travelling to Scunthorpe United on November 14.

#1905. Scott Bain on Scotland No.1 hopes, beating Celtic and his love for Falkirk

Falkirk's stunning 2-0 win over Celtic was built on discipline, resilience and a goalkeeping performance that Scott Bain admits ranks among the very best of his career.

The former Celtic keeper was in inspired form against his old club, producing a string of saves as John McGlynn's side claimed a famous victory over the Premiership champions. The result stretched Falkirk's winning run to four games and delivered a third consecutive clean sheet, with Bain at the heart of it all.

Having spent seven years at Celtic, where he was often a spectator for long spells, the 34-year-old relished being called into action and believed the display showcased the best of his shot-stopping ability.

"It was a busy day. It was an amazing result, four wins in a row and three clean sheets in a row. Amazing for the team, amazing for the club and the manager and, for myself, just delighted with the performance.

"We can take so much belief from that game. I really enjoyed the game. I had an early save and then one just before half-time from Duran. When we came out in the second half I thought it was going to be backs against the wall.

"I thought we defended excellently. We put our bodies in front of things, we cleared things and I just felt it was one of those games where they weren't going to score. Thankfully they never.

"When it got to about the 77th minute I thought we were going to be fine. They put us under a lot of pressure and put balls in the box, but I thought our togetherness, our team spirit and also our quality when we won the ball back at times was excellent.

"We outfought them at times and we also outplayed them at times. It was really good."

When asked if it was the finest display of his career, Bain admitted Sunday's performance was certainly in the conversation.

"It was probably the most saves I've made in a game. I had one against Dundee United that was similar this season where we never really managed to hold on.

"But I thought there we looked really comfortable in the end, although I'm having to make these saves.

"When it got down to the nitty-gritty of the last five minutes I thought we looked quite comfortable."

Bain's form has not gone unnoticed. Falkirk supporters repeatedly sang his name during the victory and even hailed him as Scotland's No.1, although the goalkeeper is not interested in making grand claims about displacing those ahead of him in the international pecking order.

The keeper, who has four Scotland caps, hopes his performances can earn him another call-up from Sebastien Pocognoli and admits he thoroughly enjoys being involved with the national squad.

"The fans have been brilliant with me," he said. "When I came here it probably took me a couple of games to get going and they stood by me. I feel really comfortable going into games and I feel like I'm performing really well, so it's nice that they sing that.

"I hope that I'm in the next squad. I really enjoyed working with the manager and seeing his ideas and how he works.

"As long as I go away and put my best foot forward, I'm happy to give my best account of myself out there."

Bain is widely regarded as one of the best ball-playing goalkeepers in Scotland, but against Celtic it was the more traditional side of his game that took centre stage.

"We didn't really play out from the back as much as we normally would, but I think it's a given that people know it's one of my strongest attributes.

"I've got most of the clubs in the bag, but sometimes I slice it off the tee.

"We never really did that. It was more about the nitty-gritty and I managed to make a lot of saves, so it was a good showcase in terms of saves. I'm really enjoying my time here and I feel really comfortable in the goals at the minute."

For now, Bain knows any Scotland ambitions depend on maintaining the level he has reached in recent weeks for a Falkirk side enjoying a strong spell of form.

"It's difficult because with international football you can only do what you can do for your club and hopefully the manager sees that and makes a decision.

"I don't ever go there expecting to play. I go there to represent myself the best I can and I play these games for Falkirk to represent myself the best I can.

"Whether that turns out with the manager giving me some game time when we're away then I'll do my best if I get the opportunity. But mostly, international football for me is about what I do here. Can I put in good performances to be in the conversation? That's really what it's about."

#1900. 'They'll be back': Scott Bain issues honest Celtic verdict after Falkirk heroics

Scott Bain knows a thing or two about Celtic crises. The goalkeeper spent almost a decade at Parkhead, with the infamous 2020/21 campaign a rare blemish on an otherwise admirable CV.

Bain won seven league titles, five Scottish Cups, and four League Cups with Celtic. He predominantly served as a back-up stopper throughout his spell at the club, registering 78 appearances in seven-and-a-half years.

He came back to haunt his ex-employers on Sunday, making nine saves as Falkirk recorded their first win over Celtic since 2007.

Martin O'Neill's side have now suffered six defeats in their last 10 matches, looking anything but a structured, effective unit.

Bain, though, insists he's seen Celtic in worse states, and that it won't 'take much' for them to once more become the 'unbeatable' team he played in.

"I feel sorry for boys in terms of it's a difficult place to be when it's not going well. But I've seen them worse," Bain said. "They've been worse and I was there when they were worse.

"So I think there's obviously overreaction at times with fans and things like that because it's a very emotional club and it's a club that's rooted deep in people's families and across generations. So they demand a lot of you.

"The only way to get through it is to stand up and puff your chest out and keep going, you can't buckle to the fans or the pressure or the results. They've been fine in the league.

"Obviously the last two results are a bit damning for them but in terms of the league I don't feel there's been any issues and I think maybe these little issues here have probably been brought on from outside noise and extra pressures on to the players.

"Obviously they've not performed as well in Europe as Celtic have recently, outwith your Champions League disasters, if I can say that."

Scott Bain greets Liam Scales after Falkirk's win over Celtic. (Image: Mark Runnacles / Shutterstock)

During what's now known as the Covid season, Bain played 23 times. It remains Celtic's only trophy-less campaign since 2009/10.

"I never felt the full brunt of it but the Covid season was really tough and that wasn't even fans in the stadium," Bain explained. "I think no fans made it even worse.

"But for the majority of my time there it's been sweet, the club was in a really good place and I think it'll maybe take a few signings here and there, a few ideas here and there and they'll be back there, I don't think it'll take much."

Bain left Celtic for Falkirk last summer. He's since become one of their most important players, earning a recall to the Scotland national team.

Inconsistency of minutes at Celtic, Bain says, made finding his peak form 'impossible'.

"When I played for Celtic we were really unbeatable when I played the majority of my games so I didn't really feel that until I came in with the signing of [Vasilis] Barkas and I played a game here and there, and I always found it difficult in general to play a game, come out of the team and play a game a few months later, play a couple of games here and come out.

"And then eventually I played a game once a year - what are you supposed to do with that? It's almost impossible."

"Could be, aye," was Bain's modest response when asked if Sunday was the best performance of his career.

Did any of his old Celtic chums, then, say anything post-match?

"They did, aye, a few expletives! No, they're obviously disappointed," Bain revealed. "It's a club that demands a lot of you.

"They created a lot of chances in the game and probably would win any sort of other game in that sense, it was just one of those days.

"But, look, I'm really tight with a lot of those boys and I've spent a lot of my life really with some of them. So they're disappointed but the boys that I know have congratulated me in terms of what a performance it was."

#1899. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1898. Chebby doubles up as Chichester City find Frome for improvement

City made one change to the starting XI as skipper Rob Hutchings once again lined up at left back with Isaac Bello on the other side and Ben Pashley in the centre alongside Ryan Davidson in front of keeper Max Evans.

James Sweet, Joe Moore, Emmett Dunn, Lucas Pattenden and Worthing loanee Matt Burgess started in midfield with top scorer Harry Bridle up front. Olly Munt, Lloyd Rowlatt, Joe Clarke, Chebby and Sweet’s brother Will warmed the bench.

Dunn got well up to head away Zack Ali’s cross four minutes in and Frome eeper Kyle Phillips cut out Pattenden’s delivery. Pashley tidied up twice as the hosts pressed.

Harry Lucas turned the ball back to his goalie ahead of Bridle before Sam Meakes was flagged offside. Two good tackles by Hutchings and Moore snuffed out Frome danger.

Bridle had a chance on 13 but couldn’t get a hit off, and Evans saved at the other end when Hopkins had a go.

It was all a bit scrappy and Moore gave away a foul on Hopkins at the mid-point and captain Sam Teale’s header was simple for Evans. The Chi No1 then took a delivery from Teale without any trouble and Pashley, who had a good game, cleared another threat.

Pattenden was booked for pushing Ali just before the half hour mark. Teale headed over the bar in the 31st minute then a City free kick went straight into Phillips’ arms.

Hopkins beat Bello and Moore on 34 but Callum Gould’s cross was ineffectual before James Sweet gave way to Rowlatt. Evans hooked clear Hutchings’ back pass and Hopkins missed out on a final touch as the Robins threatened.

Evans beat Archie Ferris to a through ball and a Pashley clearance cannoned off an opponent for a Lillywhites’ goal kick, then Zac Drew fouled Hutchings. In time added on a super tackle denied Bridle.

The home side dominated the opening five minutes of the second half. Evans denied the hard-working Hopkins twice on 47 before Hutchings headed away a Meakes’ cross and Drew bought a foul on the edge of the box in the 48th minute.

Hopkins steered home Meakes’ delivery for the opening goal in the 50th minute.

Drew went into the referee’s notebook in the 54th minute for fouling Pashley, then Pattenden was flagged offside and a Robins coach got booked before theatrics from Meakes and Dunn led to a City free kick.

Chebby came on for Bridle on 58, which would prove a game-changing managerial move.

The home side also made two changes before Brendan Holmes crossed dangerously. Dunn levelled in the 65th minute, lashing home from inside the area.

Munt replaced Burgess on 71 and soon Chebby put Chi 2-1 up with a lovely strike in the 73rd minute.

Clarke came on for Moore before fantastic body strength and a decent finish by Chebby made it 3-1 on 79 minutes before the Robins threw the dice and made a triple substitution.

The home side pulled one back on 86 through new signing Corey Evans. Chi’s own Evans spectacularly denied Frome sub Jon Davies, and the visitors cleared a long Warren Maidment throw.

Chebby, on a hat-trick, struck the post with practically the last kick.

#1897. Tottenham transfer news: Forgotten £50m outcast now given fresh hope of Spurs escape in January

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 07:43

Richarlison could finally be handed a route out of Tottenham Hotspur after Trabzonspor renewed their interest in signing the Brazilian forward.

The 29-year-old has fallen out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi and has been left outside the club's first-team plans following a frustrating summer transfer window.

With Spurs now reportedly willing to accept a reduced fee, January could represent their final opportunity to secure a transfer before his contract expires.

According to reports in Turkey (via Sport Witness), Trabzonspor have not given up on signing Richarlison and could make another attempt during the January transfer window.

It is reported that the Turkish side are considering a renewed approach, although they must first create space in their foreign-player quota.

Ruslan Malinovskyi and Paul Onuachu are among the players who could make way, with Trabzonspor's financial position and squad planning also likely to influence their decision.

Galatasaray are understood to be interested too, with both Turkish clubs working behind the scenes to explore a potential deal.

Tottenham are reportedly prepared to accept around €10m (£8.5m) in January, significantly less than the €20m (£17m) they requested during the summer. That represents a considerable reduction for a player who cost Spurs around £50m, but his situation has become increasingly difficult.

Richarlison has failed to secure a move despite interest from England, Turkey and Brazil, and De Zerbi has subsequently left him outside his core plans, with the forgotten forward restricted to involvement with the U21s.

Spurs also reportedly missed out on signing Marseille's Amine Gouiri because they were unable to offload either Richarlison or Dominic Solanke.

Richarlison's Tottenham career has become a frustrating combination of inconsistent performances, failed transfers and a breakdown in his relationship with the club.

The Brazilian has struggled to establish himself as the first-choice striker, while public disagreements over his future have further complicated matters.

He reportedly rejected the opportunity to sign a contract extension, leaving Spurs facing the prospect of losing him for nothing when his deal expires in summer 2027.

Several potential exits collapsed during the summer, including interest from former club Everton and Brazilian side Vasco da Gama, while his exclusion from De Zerbi's plans has left him in limbo.

A January departure now appears increasingly sensible for all parties. Tottenham can recover a modest fee, Richarlison can pursue regular first-team football, and De Zerbi can move on from a difficult situation.

Trabzonspor still have obstacles to overcome, but the reduced asking price could finally make an agreement possible.

#1894. Why Rangers must turn late semi-final heroics into platform for success as Hampden return vindicates transfer

Rangers have spent much of the season searching for consistency, but their latest visit to Hampden provided further evidence that Derek McInnes’ squad are beginning to understand what is required when the pressure is at its highest.

Following the statement victory over Celtic in the Premier Sports Cup quarter-final, there was an expectation that Rangers would carry that momentum into their last-four meeting with Aberdeen. They duly delivered, although the nature of their narrow 1-0 triumph in Mount Florida was perhaps more indicative of the qualities required to win trophies than any display of attacking flair.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was not an evening for extravagance. Instead, Rangers had to show patience, determination and the mental strength to keep searching for a breakthrough. That moment eventually arrived in the 83rd minute through Ryan Naderi and the man who provided the assist, James Penrice, believes such attributes are becoming increasingly evident within the squad and are helping to foster a winning mentality.

“When you're on the pitch and you play for Rangers, you should go until the end of the game,” he said. “You've seen that a couple of times. The resilience to keep going to the end, keep pushing. They made it very hard for us, but I think we got our reward. Ryan gets his strikers goal and it's a massive positive.”

Having already swept Celtic aside, Rangers knew the importance of backing up that emphatic 3-0 victory. Defeat in the semi-final against a struggling Dons side would have undermined much of the positivity generated by their quarter-final success, making the assignment another significant test of their character and credentials.

Penrice acknowledged that reaching Hampden was particularly important for those members of the squad experiencing such an occasion for the first time. He believes the occasion will provide added motivation ahead of their return to the national stadium in six weeks’ time, when they will be expected to justify their favourites' billing against Hibs.

“That was big. For a lot of the boys, it's their first time being at Hampden,” stated the 27-year-old. “It's massive that they experience that and it will help them want it more. It's special seeing boys that haven't seen those kind of scenes before, haven't seen Rangers at Hampden. It can only help us, and I think it will be ten times that if you were to come back here and win it. So that's the motivation for the boys is to relive that again.”

That appetite for success could prove a major factor in the weeks ahead. Rangers now have another outing at Hampden to anticipate in mid-December, but former Hearts man Penrice is under no illusion that reaching the final guarantees anyone a place in the starting XI. Quite the opposite, in fact.

With several players edging closer to a return from injury, competition for places is expected to intensify, ensuring nobody can afford to become complacent. It is a scenario Penrice welcomes.

“When you come back here in six weeks, everyone should be pushing. Pushing to try and get in the starting 11, pushing to get on the bench,” he explained. “You need two or three players in each position fighting for a jersey. And good enough to fight for a jersey. All wanting to win, all wanting to play and I think that's the main thing.”

Penrice has also shown a willingness to embrace a different challenge, having been deployed in midfield on a couple of occasions despite being more accustomed to operating in defence. His readiness to adapt to an unfamiliar role underlines his determination to contribute wherever required.

“It was obviously not what I've been used to in a two. But when the gaffer says play there, there's no question I'll play wherever,” he declared. “Whatever I can do to help the team is what I'll do. Obviously, it's not a position I've played in before in the past for Livingston and Partick. But if he asks me to play in there, I'm going to say yes. I could play anywhere.”

That mentality will be essential. While being favourites to lift the trophy inevitably brings expectation, it also carries responsibility, and having negotiated the semi-final hurdle, they must now prove they can deliver when silverware is at stake.

Reaching a cup final so early in his Ibrox career offered Penrice further confirmation that his decision to move to Ibrox from AEK Athens in the summer was the right one.

“It was never in doubt. Never,” he exclaimed. “It was the only place I wanted to go in the summer. And I pushed hell of a lot. This is why I wanted to come here and play for a massive club and play in games like a final. It only backs up my decision.”

#1891. Man Utd sent Bruno Fernandes price tag warning as big-money club prepare fresh £45m January bid

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 08:10

Manchester United could face a significant decision over Bruno Fernandes' future, with Al-Hilal reportedly preparing a fresh offer for their captain in January.

However, former Chelsea striker Tony Cascarino believes Premier League clubs would be unwilling to pay £60m for the Portuguese midfielder, raising questions over his market value.

With Fernandes' contract situation unresolved and growing doubts about his future at Old Trafford, a departure next year is increasingly plausible.

Al-Hilal have revived their interest in Fernandes and are prepared to offer €55m (£45m) as early as January.

That could provide United with an opportunity to cash in on their captain, whose contract is approaching its final months, although the club reportedly have an option to extend it by another year.

Cascarino, speaking on talkSPORT's Weekend Sports Breakfast, questioned whether any Premier League side would pay up to £60m for the 32-year-old.

He acknowledged Fernandes' importance to United over several seasons but argued that his age, wages and recent form would make such a fee difficult to justify for a domestic rival.

"You might from Saudi Arabia, but you wouldn't from another Premier League team - there is no way that would happen," Cascarino said.

Fernandes' relationship with Michael Carrick has also come under scrutiny after he questioned United's pressing approach following their 4-1 defeat to Como. He was subsequently dropped to on the bench against AFC Bournemouth before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea.

Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda believes the midfielder's time at Old Trafford is coming to an end.

Speaking to talkSPORT Breakfast, he suggested that a separation could benefit both Fernandes and United, arguing that the midfielder would have a better opportunity to compete for major honours at a more established club.

The signs increasingly point towards Fernandes leaving United, particularly with uncertainty over his contract and the club's continued struggles.

Al-Hilal's reported £45m interest could offer United a financially attractive solution, especially when Premier League clubs may be reluctant to match that valuation for a 32-year-old on substantial wages.

Fernandes has been an outstanding servant, regularly producing goals and assists during difficult periods, but United may need a fresh start as they look to rebuild their squad.

There is still a possibility that his contract option is activated, but that would not necessarily guarantee he remains beyond January.

Ultimately, a Saudi move could suit all parties, while Fernandes may benefit from joining a team with a clearer direction and greater immediate ambitions.

#1890. Scotland squad: Two key players set to return, one major injury worry and Ryan Gauld wildcard

Sebastien Pocognoli names his next Scotland squad on Tuesday for two Nations League matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Scotland sit third in Group B1 on four points and are unable to catch leaders Switzerland, who have an 100 per cent record on 12 points. The Scots will be keen to catch Slovenia in second place, who are three point ahead. However, at least four points are required to give Pocognoli and Co a chance of doing so.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

North Macedonia visit Hampden on Friday, November 13 before Scotland head to St Gallen on Monday, November 16 to conclude their campaign against the Swiss. We take a look at the players would could make the squad:

Pocognoli named four goalkeepers in his squad for the first international window and given the dearth of options in this area of the team, there are unlikely to be any changes.

Angus Gunn has the gloves, but there is some debate as to whether he should remain as Scotland’s No 1 despite featuring regularly at club level for San Jose Earthquakes. Scott Bain’s excellent performance at the weekend for Falkirk against Celtic strengthened his case, while Jon McCracken has kept 12 clean sheets for Bradford City this season.

Liam Kelly was the other keeper picked last time out and given his inactivity at Rangers, he looks the most vulnerable of the quartet.

Pocognoli handed debuts to centre-halves Stephen Welsh, Luis Binks and Luke Graham last time out. Given all three are playing regularly for the clubs, they are expected to keep their place in the squad. Jack Hendry is another who is set for a call-up, but Scott McKenna is likely to miss out after picking up a back strain while playing for Dinamo Zagreb. That could open the door to Ryan Porteous at LAFC, or Wrexham’s Dom Hyam.

At right-back, Aaron Hickey, Nathan Patterson and Colby Donovan are in line for call-ups, while on the other flank, captain Andy Robertson, Kieran Tierney and Josh Doig are in pole position to be included.

If Robertson plays the next two Scotland matches, he will move on to 103 appearances and become the country’s most capped player, surpassing Sir Kenny Dalglish.

The big news is that Scott McTominay is primed for a recall after missing the last camp due to minor heart surgery. The 29-year-old has started the past seven matches for Napoli, scoring four goals, and is set to work with Pocognoli for the first time.

McTominay’s club-mate Billy Gilmour was an integral part of Pocognoli’s midfield and is fit, while fellow Serie A midfielder Lewis Ferguson started every game in the last international break and has regained first-choice status at Bologna.

John McGinn missed a penalty for Aston Villa at the weekend but has performed well at club level over the past few weeks and he is likely to be joined by Ryan Christie in the squad. If there is one more midfield berth, Kenny McLean is more likely to get it than Lennon Miller - who didn’t feature at all in the last international break - and uncapped Blackburn man Kristi Montgomery.

A wildcard could be Ryan Gauld, who is fully fit at Vancouver Whitecaps and has scored three goals in his past four matches.

Ben Gannon-Doak’s game-time for in-form Bournemouth has been limited to League Cup and European matches, but the 20-year-old has impressed when called upon by manager Marco Rose. He remains Scotland’s biggest threat out wide.

Josh McPake has had a rough schedule with Hearts but after winning his first cap last time out against Slovenia, he has done enough to keep his spot. Team-mate Calvin Miller may also have been in the running for inclusion, but he faces a spell on the sidelines due to a knee issue.

Findlay Curtis has struggled for starts at Rangers, but should Pocognoli want a third winger, he is the most likely to get the nod.

Che Adams was absent last time out due to a muscle strain, but four goals for Torino so far in Serie A suggests he is No 9 in form and it would be a surprise should he not be included.

Much was made of Oli McBurnie’s composure in front of goal - he is zero from 20 caps in terms of goals - but he continues to lead the line well for Hull City in the Premier League and scored a free-kick at the weekend.

Robbie Ure has scored one goal and provided two assists recently for Sevilla and should stay involved, while Kieron Bowie did enough in the last international camp with his excellent goal in North Macedonia. He flits in and out of the Sassuolo starting XI right now.

Ross Stewart fired a reminder to Pocognoli by scoring for Swansea at the weekend and could be a wildcard selection, while Hearts’ James Wilson will hope to stay in the plans too, although he has dropped out of the Tynecastle starting XI.

Middlesbrough are flying at the top of the Championship and Tommy Conway, who can play through the middle or out wide, has started their past three matches.

#1889. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

One of the new laws brought in this season is to speed up throw-ins and Gray falls foul of taking too long, with Charlton then being given the throw-in.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1888. ‘Forever in our hearts’: Football club remembers Crawley teenager Leo Firth

Gatwick Warriors FC announced his death in a heartfelt tribute, describing him as the 'kindest soul, with the warmest heart'.

Leo, 19, was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia when he was 16.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

His family had been searching for specialist treatments or clinical trials after being told there were no further treatment options available to him at the Royal Marsden.

Paying tribute on Facebook, Gatwick Warriors FC said: “Our Warrior has flown up high after a long and courageous battle with cancer.

“Leo is the true definition of a warrior and he will be sorely missed by his family, his friends, his teammates and everyone here at the club."

In a memorial message accompanying the post, the club said: “It is with great sadness, that we have to share our Warrior flew up high after battling for many years. The kindest soul, with the warmest heart.

“Leo will be truly missed by us all at the club. Please join us in offering our condolences and support to his family and friends at this difficult time. Forever in our hearts.”

Leo’s mum, Ashleigh Francis, said chemotherapy had initially put his cancer into remission for 18 months.

After the disease returned, he underwent further chemotherapy, radiotherapy and a cord blood stem cell transplant. His mum said the leukaemia returned again seven months after the transplant, and two rounds of the Apollo clinical trial had failed to work.

His sister, Ellie Firth, set up a fundraiser to help the family explore potential treatments and specialist advice, as well as fulfil Leo’s wishes and create memories together.

Gatwick Warriors ended its tribute with the words: “We love you, we miss you and whenever we kick a ball we’ll be doing it in your honour."

#1887. England squad announcement: When will Thomas Tuchel confirm squad for November international break?

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 08:34, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 08:38

Thomas Tuchel’s England are back in action this month as they resume their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

After finishing third at this summer’s World Cup, the Three Lions won three of their opening four League A Group C fixtures across an 11-day period during the September/October international break.

England responded to their matchday one defeat at home to world champions Spain (3-2) by smashing Croatia 7-0 in between two more victories without reply against the Czech Republic.

With two more games on the horizon, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about England's latest squad announcement.

Tuchel will announce his England squad ahead of the upcoming international break at 10am on Friday, November 6.

The Three Lions boss is then expected to hold a press conference on the same day to explain the decisions he has made.

A 27-man squad was initially named by Tuchel in September, though a number of high-profile names eventually pulled out.

Six days after Tuchel's squad announcement, England will welcome Croatia to Wembley Stadium for their penultimate League A Group C fixture at 7.45pm on November 12.

The Three Lions will conclude their Nations League group with a trip to Riyadh Air Metropolitano – Atletico Madrid’s home stadium – where they will face Spain at 7.45pm (GMT) on November 15.

England currently sit second in League A Group C with nine points from their opening four matches, three behind leaders Spain who boast a 100% record.

The Three Lions also sit six points clear ahead of Croatia in third and know that either a draw or victory against the Checkered Ones would guarantee a top-two finish in the group.

The top-two teams in all four groups in League A will progress to the quarter-finals; Spain have already qualified with two games to spare but could still be pipped to top spot by England.

Group winners are seeded for the quarter-final draw, meaning they will be drawn against a runner-up from another group and will also host the second leg of their two-legged tie.

Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane is set to return to international action for the first time since winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

Already the nation's all-time top scorer with 91 goals, Kane will aim to surpass Peter Shilton (125) to become England's most-capped men’s player in history.

#1885. The names of TV licence evaders from across Sussex prosecuted by HMCTS Single Justice Service in October

HMCTS Single Justice Service records results handled by various courts prosecuting people from across England.

The names of those prosecuted are made public in court documents regularly released to the press.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Those who admit using a television set without a licence and those found guilty at court are fined, and end up with a criminal record.

The annual licence is £180, with discounts for certain groups.

Every household that watches live television or live streaming, including on laptops or mobile devices, needs a TV licence.

The licence funds the BBC’s output including TV and radio, podcasts, Bitesize, the website, apps and the iPlayer. The corporation says that every week, 90 per cent of UK adults use at least one of its services.

People who do not buy a licence, but watch live TV, are prosecuted at magistrates’ courts under the Communications Act 2003. It is a summary-only offence, punishable by a fine of up to £1,000, and can only be heard by magistrates. Non-payers cannot be jailed, but those who repeatedly refuse to pay fines imposed by the courts can be jailed under separate legislation.

Here are the latest successful prosecutions for using a television set without a licence that took place in recent weeks from across Sussex.

#1884. Slavia Prague vs Arsenal - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 02 Nov 2026 09:52, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 10:14

An Arsenal team yet to suffer defeat in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase take on a Slavia Prague side still searching for their first triumph of the tournament at the Fortuna Arena on Wednesday evening.

The Gunners have collected seven points from the first nine on offer in Europe, whereas their Czech hosts have just one draw and two defeats to show from their opening three fixtures.

No longer perfect points-wise or rearguard-wise in the Champions League, Arsenal ventured to Bayern Munich on matchday three as the only team in the UCL yet to concede a goal, having shut out Lille and Napoli in the opening two rounds.

However, the Premier League champions still went toe to toe with their Bavarian counterparts and came away with a hard-earned point from an enthralling 2-2 draw with Bayern, replicating an incredibly rare and eerie feat in the process.

The four-goal stalemate marked just the second time that Arsenal had scored first, fallen behind and still managed to avoid defeat in a European Cup/Champions League fixture, after an identical result against none other than Bayern in 2024.

While Arsenal's 14-game winning sequence in the league phase may now be a thing of the past, the Gunners remain in the coveted top eight spots of the league-phase table, and two goals conceded still makes them the joint-best defensive side in the competition, alongside Stuttgart and PSV Eindhoven.

The elusive quadruple remains a pipe dream after their embarrassing EFL Cup exit to Fleetwood Town, but Mikel Arteta got the seismic response he was hoping for on Sunday, overseeing a long-awaited Premier League victory at Anfield.

Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool - their first in the top flight away to the Reds in 14 years - took them three points clear at the top of the Premier League table, and highlighted the gap that remains between the champions and their challengers.

Involved in their own frenetic four-goal draw on matchday three - albeit in differing circumstances - Slavia Prague put their first Champions League point on the board courtesy of coming from 2-0 down to hold Fenerbahce in Istanbul.

Jindrich Trpisovsky's men may have feared a hiding when Oguz Aydin and Mason Greenwood struck inside the opening 11 minutes, but Lukas Provod swiftly cut the deficit in half before Pavel Kacor's 90th-minute leveller ended their European losing sequence.

Slavia had fallen to Lens and Sabah in their opening two fixtures, but their gritty draw at Fenerbahce was not enough to lift them out of the automatic elimination places, as Wednesday's hosts lie 32nd in the 36-team rankings after three matchdays.

The Red and Whites have also now failed to win in a staggering 18 consecutive UEFA fixtures - coincidentally the same length as Arsenal's unbeaten UCL run, excluding penalties - but Trpisovsky's crop have found form again at an ideal time.

Indeed, Slavia Prague have now strung together a five-game unbeaten run in all tournaments and have won back-to-back fixtures, most recently demolishing Jablonec 5-0 to maintain a seven-point lead at the top of the Czech First League table.

However, the reigning national champions were swept aside 3-0 by Arsenal at home in the 2025-26 league phase and have failed to win any of their previous five head-to-heads against the Gunners, whose 7-0 thumping of Slavia in 2007 remains their joint-biggest victory in European football.

Arsenal quartet Christos Tzolis, Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori all battled back from injury concerns to make the trip to Anfield, but Bukayo Saka (quad) and William Saliba (back) remain absent.

Eberechi Eze is also a fresh concern after Arteta revealed that the Englishman is dealing with an unspecified fitness problem, but Max Dowman - serving a three-game domestic suspension - is available here.

Given Eze's concern, Tzolis's fast-tracked comeback and Madueke's recent ankle scare, it would not be a shock to see Dowman start on Wednesday evening, as Arteta makes a handful of alterations across the park.

Meanwhile, Slavia have a handful of fitness concerns to take into account for the visit of Arsenal, including experienced winger Ivan Schranz, who has been laid low by an illness for weeks.

Star attacker Lukas Provod also missed the thrashing of Jablonec and is a doubt, as is defender Ange N'Guessan, who came off with an unspecified injury last time out.

From injuries to suspensions, 6ft 7in striker Tomas Chory has been banished by manager Trpisovsky after showing a referee the middle finger during a recent Czech First League fixture against Hradec Kralove; he is not expected to play for the club again.

Domchak; Vlcek, Holes, Zima; Suleiman, Moses, Sadilek, Kubiak; Ayaosi, Sturm; Nowak

Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Dowman, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres

After Arsenal's second-string team failed to beat a fourth-tier side in the EFL Cup, Arteta should resist the urge to make wholesale changes against a Slavia side whose momentum is growing.

Nevertheless, the Czech champions have been carved open at will in Europe - shipping seven goals thus far - so we can envisage Arsenal replicating their three-goal success from last season.

#1883. Horsham FC record biggest ever National League South win after five-star showing at Farnborough – the match in 51 pictures

The ruthless Hornets served up a Halloween treat for their supporters as they stormed to a 5-0 win at Cherrywood Road on Saturday.

Horsham went ahead in the 43rd minute courtesy of a delicious James Hammond free-kick. Greg Luer then added the Hornets’ second on the stroke of half-time after good work from Charlie Hester-Cook to win the ball deep in Farnborough territory.

George Cox made it three with a ferocious 25-yard piledriver on 74 minutes before Reece Myles-Meekums poked home from close-range for Horsham’s fourth four minutes later.

Substitute Harvey Sparks then added the icing on the cake in second half stoppage time to confirm the Hornets’ biggest ever win at step two.

The thumping victory moved Horsham up to tenth in the table – and to within two points of the play-off places.

The Hornets visit SCFL Premier outfit Pagham in the Sussex Transport Senior Cup tomorrow evening.

#1882. Barnsley FC defender and ex-Cambridge United man Jubril Okedina keen to 'explode' in new chapter

Barnsley defender Jubril Okedina is keen to see his career “explode” following a difficult period.

A product of Tottenham Hotspur’s academy, Okedina jumped straight into senior EFL football when it became apparent there was no first-team pathway for him in North London.

He saw a loan move to Cambridge United made permanent and went on spend four full seasons with the club in League One, racking up over 100 appearances for the U’s.

A spell with Bohemians followed his Cambridge exit in the summer of 2025, but the 26-year-old left the Republic of Ireland having made just three appearances.

He has been given a fresh start in South Yorkshire, where the Malawi international is looking to lay down roots.

"100 per cent [I would like to make Barnsley a home],” Okedina said. "I feel like Barnsley is a massive club and it's a great opportunity for me. It's the type of club that I wanted to join, [the type] I've always imagined myself joining.

"I really want to take this opportunity and really explode in this part of my career.”

Okedina was an unlikely hero at the weekend, entering the fray from the bench after just 12 minutes in Barnsley’s 1-1 draw with Oxford United.

Jack Shepherd’s dismissal ushered Okedina into the thick of it and he was deployed at right-back by Reds head coach Daniel Stendel.

Not only did Okedina defend with remarkable grit, he provided the assist for Vimal Yoganathan’s opener.

"I was ready to come on from literally any minute,” said Okedina. “I've seen Shep confronted by the referee, so I just got up straight away, did some sprints.

"I've come on in games before, so I was prepared to come on for this game as well."

Okedina has not yet started a league game for the Reds but undoubtedly staked a claim for a starting spot with his display against Oxford.

“I've gelled in well with the team, with the gaffer, the coaches,” he said. “And I've enjoyed every moment of it.

“Even though it's not been positive in results, we're all positive and we're working hard to change that for sure.”

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium.
